newsitem.title: GERMANY: Munich Re reveals small corp. stakes.
newsitem.headline: Munich Re reveals small corp. stakes.

text.p: Muenchener Rueckversicherungs AG, the world's largest reinsurer, on Wednesday said the total market value of its corporate shareholdings below five percent was 5.16 billion marks.

The reinsurer, known as Munich Re, was giving details for the first time on its small stakes, the most valuable of which include holdings in Deutsche Bank AG and Dresdner Bank AG and chemical group Bayer AG.

Munich Re has already given details of its larger corporate stakes, which include a 26 percent holding in German insurer Allianz AG Holding, which released details of its small shareholdings just last week.
Munich Re said last month it had agreed to reveal the smaller stakes in response to a court order following a complaint from one of its shareholders.
Munich Re noted that its total investments as at June 30 1996 were around 120 billion marks. Each of its sixteen smaller corporate shareholdings had a market value of more than 100 million marks.
The group said it owned a 1.5 percent stake in Deutsche worth 537 million marks, 2.3 percent of Dresdner worth 401 million and 1.7 percent of Bayer, worth 632 million marks.

The list also included British composite insurer Commercial Union Plc, in which Munich Re said it had a 4.4 percent stake with a market value of 378 million marks and Dutch insurer Fortis/AMEV, in which it owns a 3.6 percent stake valued at 282 million.
